findings.text: The action-handler path now emits `command:<name>` on `this.parent` instead of `this`. A listener attached to the command itself, such as `sub.on('command:sub', fn)`, no longer fires. The root program (no parent) also never emits, so `program.on('command:prog')` with an action handler is silently dropped.

The new `else if` branch fires when the parent has a listener for `command:<name>`, even if this command has no action handler. It runs before the `operands.length` branch, so unknown-subcommand handling is skipped. For a parent listening on `command:foo`, `foo bar` (where `bar` is not a subcommand) emits the event and never reaches the `*` handler, the `command:*` listener or `unknownCommand`. A command with neither an action handler nor subcommands also hits this branch, so the help/unknown-command fallthrough is bypassed.

0.reason: Emitting the legacy `command:<name>` event on the parent is deliberate: the documented pattern is `program.on('command:sub')`, and the root program has no parent command event to emit, so this restores the intended behaviour rather than breaking it.

1.reason: On purpose, a parent listener on `command:<name>` acts like an action handler for that command (legacy support), so dispatching to it before the unknown-command and help fallbacks is by design.
